technical_and_design_decisions: U1 shell: implement on top of Spring Shell; invoke the s-c-d REST API using a HATEOAS-aware client (e.g., Spring HATEOAS Traverson over RestTemplate) so the shell follows links exposed by the server rather than hard-coding URIs.

U7 stream REST support: implement a Spring MVC @RestController (StreamController) exposing HATEOAS resources for stream definition, deployment, undeployment, destruction, listing, and status; delegate to stream definition/deployment domain services; consistent error handling via @ControllerAdvice.

U2 redis counter: port the Spring XD redis counter as a standalone Spring Boot application module using the spring-cloud-stream binder abstraction; Redis access via Spring Data Redis; module packaged per spring-cloud-stream-modules conventions.

U5 bootified ModuleLauncher: convert ModuleLauncher to a Spring Boot application using auto-configuration and @ConfigurationProperties with relaxed binding for module/launch options, replacing ad-hoc argument parsing.

U4 external module dependencies: extend the Boot loader approach (PropertiesLauncher-style) with a module resolver that resolves module-dependent JARs (e.g., JDBC drivers) from Maven repositories at launch time and places them on the launched module's classpath, keeping them out of the OOTB module archives.

U6 PHD/HDFS: handle as a time-boxed investigation spike (classloader isolation options, dependency shading vs. root-classpath loading); deliverable is a written recommendation and, if needed, a small proof of concept - no production code.
U3/U8 CI: configure CI plans (Maven-based) that trigger on every commit, run unit and integration tests, publish snapshots/artifacts to a repository, and notify on failures.
Build with Maven (multi-module for s-c-s-m); testing with JUnit, Spring Test, and MockMvc for the REST layer; embedded/in-memory infrastructure used in tests where feasible (e.g., embedded Redis).
assumptions: A single developer (the estimator) performs all work; estimates are effort (work-hours), not elapsed calendar time, and include design, implementation, unit/integration tests, and developer documentation for each activity.
The s-c-d, s-c-s, and spring-cloud-stream-modules repositories already exist with basic project scaffolding; no greenfield repository or legal/open-source setup work is required.
A CI server instance (e.g., Jenkins/Concourse/Bamboo) and the necessary credentials and permissions are available; no procurement or server installation effort is included.
A Redis instance (or embedded Redis) is available for development and integration testing of the counter module.
The U6 spike is validated via design analysis and a local proof of concept; access to a full PHD/HDFS cluster is not required.
No UI work is in scope; the increment covers the REST API, the shell client, module ports/adaptations, launcher work, and CI only.
Stories U1-U8 constitute the complete software increment; no additional features or hardening beyond what is listed is included.

The technology baseline is the one implied by the stories (Spring Boot, Spring Cloud Stream/Data, Spring Shell, Spring Data Redis). The generic Spring Framework 6.0 / Java 17 note in the specification does not materially change the estimates.
Code review happens within the activities; a final cross-story integration and verification activity is included separately.

activities.activity_name: U1 - Design shell and REST client approach
activities.activity_description: Choose Spring Shell version, design command model for stream operations, and set up the HATEOAS-aware REST client (authentication, root-resource discovery, error mapping) used by the shell to invoke StreamController operations.
Implement shell commands for stream create/define, deploy, undeploy, destroy, list, and status, including argument/option handling, tab-completion hints, and formatted output of server responses.

activities.activity_name: U1 - Shell integration tests and docs
activities.activity_description: Write integration tests that run the shell against a live s-c-d server to validate StreamController operations end-to-end, plus user-facing command documentation.

activities.activity_name: U2 - Analyze XD redis counter and design s-c-s module
activities.activity_description: Review the Spring XD redis counter implementation (options, semantics, Redis usage) and design the equivalent spring-cloud-stream module: binder binding, configuration properties, and counter update/retrieve semantics for dashboard feeding.
Implement the standalone Spring Boot counter module using spring-cloud-stream binder abstraction and Spring Data Redis, including configuration properties and counter store/service logic.

activities.activity_name: U2 - Counter module tests and docs
activities.activity_description: Write unit and integration tests (embedded/local Redis, binder test support) verifying counting semantics, and add module metadata/README documentation.

activities.activity_name: U3 - CI pipeline for spring-cloud-data repo
activities.activity_description: Configure the CI plan for the s-c-d repository: build triggered on every commit, Maven build with unit/integration test execution and reporting, artifact publishing to the snapshot repository, and failure notifications.

Research and design how module-dependent JARs (e.g., database drivers) are resolved (Maven coordinates) and added to the launched module's classpath via a Boot loader extension, without embedding them in OOTB module archives.
Implement the module resolver and Boot loader (PropertiesLauncher-style) changes that resolve dependent JARs at launch time and construct the module classloader accordingly.

activities.activity_name: U4 - Tests with sample external JAR and docs
activities.activity_description: Verify the approach with a representative external dependency (e.g., a JDBC driver) via integration tests, and document how operators declare module dependencies.
Refactor ModuleLauncher into a Spring Boot application: auto-configuration, @ConfigurationProperties with relaxed binding for module and launcher settings, replacing manual option parsing.

activities.activity_name: U5 - Migrate option handling and tests
activities.activity_description: Migrate existing module launch option handling to Boot property binding, preserve backward-compatible behavior, and update/add unit and integration tests.

Time-boxed investigation of approaches for supporting the HDFS module with PHD as provider: analyze classloader isolation, dependency shading, and root-classpath loading options; build a small proof of concept; document findings and a recommendation.

Define REST resources, URIs, representations, and HATEOAS links for stream commands (create/define, deploy, undeploy, destroy, list, status) and the error model, consistent with s-c-d API conventions.

Implement the StreamController @RestController endpoints backed by stream definition and deployment services, including request validation, resource assemblers, pagination for list, and exception handling.

activities.activity_name: U7 - REST tests and API documentation
activities.activity_description: Write MockMvc and integration tests covering success and error paths for all stream endpoints, and produce REST API documentation (endpoints, payloads, examples).

activities.activity_name: U8 - CI pipeline for spring-cloud-stream-modules repo
activities.activity_description: Configure the CI plan for the multi-module s-c-s-m repository: per-commit Maven builds across all modules, test execution and reporting, per-module artifact publishing, and failure notifications.

Cross-story integration: verify shell against the new REST API end-to-end, run full builds on both CI pipelines, resolve integration issues, and perform final code review and release-readiness checks for the increment.
